career_archive_entry.speaker: narrator
career_archive_entry.text: The conservation workroom smelled of starch, clean cloth and the pears somebody had hidden behind a sample chest. Tan Ke offered Yue a stool with a repaired rung. 'You have worked in this archive before,' she said. 'That saves you learning where the kettle lives. It does not save you learning this.' Yue sat carefully. After the river's unfinished losses, the possibility of becoming useful at a quieter bench felt almost indecently attractive.

career_archive_induction_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_01.text: Luo brought the appointment sheet instead of another household case. Yue's earlier public or stewardship service remained its own settled work, with its own actual terms. This was a new conservation-trainee contract. It did not revive a declined post or borrow the old one-person appropriation. 'One career intake,' Luo said. 'If you spend this term here, the other intake places remain for other people.' Yue touched the blank line where her name would go.

career_archive_induction_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_02.text: The new board appropriation was one hundred copper: forty for ten completed trainee work shifts, twelve for the independent examiner, twelve for materials, twenty-four for qualified cover and twelve in reserve. Four copper paid each accepted shift. Accommodation came under a separate existing hostel arrangement and was not charged to this purse. The reserve could not quietly become extra wages or a public reading grant. Yue liked how small the figure looked until she imagined earning it.

career_archive_induction_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_03.text: Tan laid a blistered scrap beside an undamaged one. Both were discarded teaching stock with no private writing. 'Your fifth stage will remain your fifth stage,' she told Yue. 'We will use your steadiness where it helps. We will not make a sixth stage out of a dry-looking page.' Yue laughed, then realized how much she had hoped there might be something she could repair by being stronger. Tan let the laugh fade without rescuing her from it.

career_archive_induction_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_04.text: The trainee appointment allowed supervised work within named permissions. It granted no treatment license, no key to private collections and no right to read the text beneath a damaged edge. A visiting board examiner would later assess a bounded assistant qualification independently of Tan's teaching. 'You may discover you dislike the work,' Tan said. 'Finding that out is also useful.' Yue wanted the certificate already. She disliked how clearly Tan could see it.

career_archive_induction_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_05.text: Sun Nian arrived at the public receiving desk with a cloth parcel and a small paper kite. The parcel contained issued reading copies she was returning under their existing arrangement. Her family originals and private notebook stayed with their custodians. The kite belonged to a child who had given her the job of testing its string. 'The papers can wait their turn,' Sun told Luo. 'The kite has a very impatient employer.'

career_archive_induction_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_06.text: Yue's first paid shift began with permission checks and empty support boards, under Tan's immediate supervision. She matched the marked boards to the public copies already authorized for handling, refusing the tempting shortcut of lifting two sheets together. By midday her shoulders ached more than they had after some glamorous qi exercises. Tan showed her how to bring the work toward her rather than bend toward it. Nobody praised the ache as evidence of dedication.

career_archive_induction_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_07.text: One copy had a split corner carrying half a printed character. Yue wanted to turn it over and discover the rest. Its receiving permission covered the condition survey, not a new textual inquiry. Tan held the sheet while Yue entered the visible split and the limitation of her view. The absence annoyed her. At the kiln, a hidden flaw had been something to expose. Here another person's boundary could properly keep something hidden.

career_archive_induction_08.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_08.text: Luo brought lunch in two bowls because the kitchen had mistaken the workroom's order for a request about paper. One bowl contained rice; the other contained an extremely earnest boiled pear. Tan examined the pear like a suspected adhesive and then ate it. Yue laughed hard enough to lose a grain down her sleeve. For a moment the future held ordinary lunches instead of examinations. She found herself wanting that future more, rather than less.

career_archive_induction_09.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_09.text: At the first shift's receiving, Tan checked Yue's actual support placements and accepted the completed list. The wage clerk paid four copper. The payment covered that work, not an imagined successful qualification at the end of the term. Yue put one coin aside for a letter home and heard it click against the others. She had often described work to her family by its dangers. She wanted to describe a stool that did not wobble.

career_archive_induction_10.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_10.text: The second shift covered supervised enclosure preparation for already released public copies. Yue measured the permitted edges through their supports and cut ordinary protective folders from the allocated stock. A ragged cut wasted one strip; Tan charged it to the real materials line without calling it a tragedy. They adjusted the cutting stop and finished the accepted batch. The next folder closed neatly. Yue enjoyed that small success with a force that surprised her.

career_archive_induction_11.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_11.text: One pupil at the public desk asked whether the new folders meant the old words had been forgiven. Luo said the folders protected paper; people had to discuss forgiveness themselves. The child considered this disappointing division of labor. Yue thought of claims that a better copy had never settled, and of private notebooks no amount of competence had made hers. She could learn an honest trade here without becoming the judge of every story the trade carried.

career_archive_induction_12.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_12.text: The second shift's accepted folders earned another four copper. Tan retained all preservation judgments, including the decision that one unstable copy needed qualified treatment outside Yue's scope. The damaged copy did not become usable because the neighboring folders looked handsome. Yue wrote home on her own purchased paper that evening. She described the pear, the waste strip and the four copper. She left her hunger for a permanent place until the last sentence.

career_archive_induction_13.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_13.text: During the third shift, Yue and Luo checked completed condition records against the copies themselves. The public titles were visible under existing access; private source papers were absent. A copied date differed from its receiving entry. Yue marked the discrepancy for its proper reviewer instead of repairing the date with a guess. Luo's familiar reserve made sense at this bench. A conservation record could preserve a question without supplying its answer.

career_archive_induction_14.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_14.text: The letter home went into the outgoing bag after Yue paid the actual posting charge from her own coins. Luo did not read it or make it an accession. Sun passed the desk carrying the kite, now with a longer tail. 'It flew badly,' she reported with satisfaction. 'We have learned exactly how badly.' Yue asked if that counted as failure. Sun asked whether she had wanted an answer or only a flattering kite.

career_archive_induction_15.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_15.text: The third shift ended with every accepted condition entry checked and the discrepant date referred. Its four copper brought induction wages to twelve for three completed shifts. Tan signed only the supervised duties Yue had performed. Yue's hands were steadier after the repeated placements and rests, but her cultivation remained at its earned fifth stage. She had joined the workroom. She had not yet earned a conservation-assistant qualification.

career_archive_induction_16.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_16.text: The practice chest came out after paid receiving, during the separately scheduled teaching interval. Its sheets were disposable blanks stained and torn for exercises. Nobody would lose a family letter if Yue made a mistake here. That reassurance lasted until Tan asked her to choose how to lift a brittle-looking corner onto a support. Yue could name three sensible cautions. Knowing their names did not make her fingers obey them.

career_archive_induction_17.speaker: narrator
career_archive_induction_17.text: Tan stepped back far enough to watch. The corner looked almost sound, except for a pale crescent under the edge. Yue remembered winning respect by carrying more than people expected. At this bench, respect might require admitting she could not tell whether the crescent was an old crease or a fresh weakness. Luo had left a pencil beside her; it bore tooth marks from some previous anxious reader. She turned it until the marks faced down.

career_archive_trial_choice.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_choice.text: The trial sheet was a marked practice blank, not entrusted material. Tan offered three approaches within the exercise: attempt the lift while the teacher watched, stop for closer inspection, or ask Tan to hold the support while Yue checked the edge. Each would reveal something different about her readiness. Stopping could use the remaining practice interval without completing a lift. Yue wanted to look competent; she also wanted to become competent.

choices.text: Attempt the watched practice lift and test the doubtful corner.
Stop the lift and spend the interval inspecting the doubtful edge.
Ask Tan to hold the support while you check and lift the edge.

career_archive_trial_fail_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_fail_01.text: Yue eased the practice corner upward before its support was fully seated. The pale crescent opened into a tear. Tan stopped the lift, but the small sound had already traveled through Yue's chest. She put her hands flat on the table. The blank had no owner's words to lose; the mistake still belonged to her. 'I thought it would hold,' she said. Tan answered, 'That is what this trial was able to find.'

career_archive_trial_fail_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_fail_02.text: The trial was recorded as failed, with the premature lift and unsupported crescent named. Tan did not certify Yue or subtract wages already earned for different completed work. The torn practice sheet went into the teaching evidence envelope, clearly marked as an exercise. Yue wanted to hide it under another scrap. A drawer seemed large enough to hide an entire future when that future depended on what people believed about her hands.

career_archive_trial_fail_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_fail_03.text: During the break, Luo sat beside her without bringing the assessment sheet. He asked whether she wanted company or silence. Yue said company, then resented him for having so little useful advice. He peeled a pear into one long strip and broke it by accident near the end. 'There goes my qualification,' he said. She laughed reluctantly. He put the peel in the rubbish instead of pretending the joke had answered her disappointment.

career_archive_trial_fail_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_fail_04.text: Tan prescribed a remediation exercise with contrasting practice edges and a fully seated support before any lift. Yue first described what she could actually see. She misclassified another crescent, this time before touching it. Tan let the wrong description remain visible, then asked her to compare the two edges through a hand lens. Yue hated the time it took. She hated more that the time was helping.

career_archive_trial_fail_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_fail_05.text: The replacement practice lift began only after Yue checked the support and stated a stopping point. She used no qi on the sheet. When the corner resisted, she set it down and asked Tan to examine it. The teacher confirmed a concealed attachment placed for the exercise. Refusal completed that trial correctly. Yue had wanted success to feel like graceful movement. This success felt like holding still while someone else knew more.

career_archive_trial_fail_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_fail_06.text: On the second remediation blank, the edge was stable and the support sat correctly. Yue completed the bounded lift, replacement and condition entry under observation. Tan accepted the repeated exercise after checking every placement. The original failed result remained on the teaching sheet beside the later pass; it did not become a first-attempt triumph. Yue asked to keep a copy of the torn blank's outline in her own notebook.

career_archive_trial_fail_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_fail_07.text: That evening, Yue drew the outline badly and wrote what she had done before the tear. She would later be asked about this failure during independent assessment. Tan recorded the extra supervised checking interval already used by the remediation within the existing cover allocation, so the error cost real training time without spending another job's purse. Yue left the workroom knowing a mistake could become evidence for learning without turning into a secret she had to guard.

career_archive_trial_stop_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_stop_01.text: Yue put down the lifting tool and said she could not classify the crescent safely. Tan asked her to show the uncertainty without touching the corner. She pointed through the support. The pause consumed the remaining lift interval; Yue would not complete that day's planned practice movement. She felt foolish standing beside an intact blank while another trainee somewhere probably made admirable progress. Tan inspected the crescent and found a deliberately weakened fiber line.

career_archive_trial_stop_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_stop_02.text: They recorded a correct stopping decision and an incomplete lift exercise. No full trial pass or qualification followed from stopping. The practice sheet remained intact, but Yue still had to demonstrate a safe movement later. She asked Tan whether caution could become a way to avoid learning anything difficult. 'Yes,' Tan said. The answer startled her more than an easy reassurance would have done.

career_archive_trial_stop_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_stop_03.text: At lunch, Sun listened while Yue described the blank without borrowing any private story as an example. Sun had once refused to fly the child's kite in a gust, then found herself refusing on an entirely calm afternoon too. 'The string was still mine to hold,' she said. 'I had begun treating the wind as an excuse.' Yue looked across the courtyard at a motionless plum branch and understood the unpleasant part.

career_archive_trial_stop_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_stop_04.text: The next practice interval used a sound blank with the same apparent crescent drawn harmlessly on its surface. Yue checked the support, examined the edge and distinguished a mark from a structural weakness. Tan asked her to name a limit she could verify rather than wait until all imaginable doubts vanished. Her limit was a small observed movement, with the blank fully supported and an immediate stop if resistance changed.

career_archive_trial_stop_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_stop_05.text: She lifted the permitted practice edge, settled it onto its support and returned it without strain. The motion was almost offensively small after the fear surrounding it. Tan checked the outcome and accepted the completed movement trial. The earlier incomplete exercise stayed incomplete in the record. Yue found she did not need to call it a success in order to stop resenting it.

career_archive_trial_stop_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_stop_06.text: The planned teaching hour had now supplied both a stopping demonstration and the necessary safe lift, across different intervals. That used the ordinary scheduled cover rather than an extra remedial interval. Tan asked Yue to explain the distinction to a new workroom helper using the disposable blanks. Yue said a stop protected the sheet, while a later checked attempt taught her something she had still needed to learn.

career_archive_trial_stop_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_stop_07.text: Her notebook gained two drawings that evening: an unstable edge she had left alone and a stable one she had moved. The independent examiner would later ask why stopping had not itself completed the lift requirement. Yue knew the answer now without reciting Tan's words. She kept the drawings loose, so she could add another explanation when her understanding grew, rather than bind this version into a permanent story about being careful.

career_archive_trial_support_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_support_01.text: Yue asked Tan to hold the support while she examined the crescent. Asking was easy until Tan agreed, at which point Yue became embarrassingly aware of using the teacher's hands. The support stopped shifting. Through the lens she saw broken fibers below the surface. She described the weakness and halted the proposed lift. Tan accepted that finding, but pointed out that Yue had not yet performed the movement requirement.

career_archive_trial_support_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_support_02.text: With another practice blank, Tan again held the support and Yue completed the bounded lift. The result was sound. The exercise recorded a supported pass with Tan's contribution named. It did not certify Yue for the same task alone. She wanted to argue that the difference was minor, then remembered how much more possible everything had felt when another pair of hands kept the board still.

career_archive_trial_support_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_support_03.text: Luo passed the doorway carrying a stack that leaned extravagantly to one side. Tan made him take two trips. He complained that the stack had been developing a personality. Yue offered to help, within the ordinary carrying limit already cleared for her. They moved the remaining released folders together. The workroom did not become less lively when help had to be named. It became harder to pretend whose effort had made a result possible.

career_archive_trial_support_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_support_04.text: Tan set a second exercise: Yue had to secure an ordinary adjustable support herself before making the small lift. The clamp held the board, not the sheet, and used no pressure near the fragile edge. Yue checked it twice because she distrusted any arrangement that looked so plain. Tan asked which movement the second check had added. Yue found none and stopped repeating it.

career_archive_trial_support_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_support_05.text: The independent practice lift went smoothly until Yue noticed a slight catch. She set the blank down, checked the support position and corrected an exposed corner before resuming within the teacher's permission. After the replacement and condition entry, Tan accepted the completed movement trial. The earlier supported result stayed honestly attributed. Yue had now demonstrated the required bounded movement without making the teacher's hands disappear from yesterday.

career_archive_trial_support_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_support_06.text: During the ordinary scheduled review, Yue explained the two attempts to the workroom helper. One proved she could coordinate safely with qualified support; the other proved she could prepare this particular stable exercise herself. Neither authorized treatment of a damaged original. The helper asked which was more impressive. Yue thought of the unstable board, then said whichever the actual job required. She sounded older than she felt.

career_archive_trial_support_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_trial_support_07.text: She wrote Tan's name beside the first practice drawing in her own notebook. Later assessment would include a question about that contribution, so Yue could not silently present the supported trial as solo work. She also drew the clamp she had finally learned to set. It looked like an ungainly beetle. She showed Tan, who said the beetle had a respectable career ahead of it if somebody remembered to check its feet.

career_archive_training_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_training_01.text: Two further paid work shifts combined supervised folder assembly with checking condition entries for stable public copies. The practice trial itself had been teaching, not a separate wage claim. Yue's hands now reached for the support before they reached for the paper. Tan still watched every handling operation and retained the judgments outside the contract. Familiarity made the work quicker, which was welcome; it also made omitted checks more tempting.

career_archive_training_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_training_02.text: A returned public copy carried a grease mark that resembled a child's thumb. Luo found the existing reading permission but no authority to ask which child had made it. Yue described the visible mark without turning it into an accusation. The copy went to Tan for the preservation decision. At the public desk a father was praising his daughter's unusually clean hands. Yue felt the delicious urge to know more and let it pass.

career_archive_training_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_training_03.text: Sun brought the kite back, flying badly in a different way. Its new tail had solved one problem and introduced another. She insisted on this distinction as the child listened. Yue asked permission to use the kite's blank spare paper for a folding demonstration. The child refused because it was reserved for a second kite. She accepted the refusal and used allocated teaching stock. Skill did not make someone else's spare things available.

career_archive_training_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_training_04.text: The first of these shifts ended with the accepted folders counted and checked. Four copper paid the completed scope. Yue had earned sixteen copper across four actual shifts so far. She bought a steamed bun with her own money and ate it outside before it cooled. Tan joined her with nothing in her hands, then confessed she had forgotten lunch. Yue split the bun because she wanted to, without entering the kindness as training.

career_archive_training_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_training_05.text: On the second shift they corrected a condition entry Yue had copied from the wrong public sheet. The two sheets were similar, but the error remained hers. She checked the actual items again under supervision and entered an explicit correction without deleting the earlier entry. The completed batch passed Tan's receiving review. Nobody used the correction to infer that the sheet's private owner had lied about its history.

career_archive_training_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_training_06.text: The second shift paid four copper, bringing training and induction wages to twenty. Yue had now finished five contracted shifts. The checked batches, corrected record and repeated safe placements were completed work; Tan entered that demonstrated growth without granting a professional certificate. The visiting examiner's two assessed work shifts were still ahead. Yue folded her wage receipt into her own pouch and left the work records where their appointed custodians kept them.

career_archive_training_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_training_07.text: Before the examiner arrived, Tan asked Yue what she wanted from a permanent trade. Yue said reliable wages, then stopped because the answer was true and incomplete. She wanted to become the person people sent for when a thing could still be saved. She wanted to leave a room and know she had made its tomorrow less cruel. Tan listened. 'You will also be sent for things that cannot be saved,' she said.

career_archive_training_08.speaker: narrator
career_archive_training_08.text: Yue slept badly after that conversation. In her dream, every paper she touched became a letter home, and every letter contained the wrong address. Morning made the dream ridiculous without making its feeling disappear. Luo handed her the examination schedule and a warmed cup. The examiner was independently appointed by the board and paid from the twelve-copper line. Tan would supervise entrusted handling but would neither set nor mark Yue's qualifying assessment.

career_archive_training_09.speaker: narrator
career_archive_training_09.text: The examiner reviewed only authorized condition records and the designated assessment copies. Yue's private letters, Sun's notebook and family originals were outside the assessment. Its eventual assistant qualification could cover condition recording, stable-paper support and enclosure work within permissions. It could not license chemical treatment, disputed custody decisions or access to confidential text. The bounded title sounded smaller than Yue's ambition. It also sounded like something she might honestly earn.

career_archive_training_10.speaker: narrator
career_archive_training_10.text: For the first assessed work shift, the examiner supplied three permitted tasks within the qualification's scope. Each had a difficult boundary: a persistent stain, an uncertain attachment or a stable sheet needing a fitted support. Yue could choose any one. The examiner would judge what she actually did and how she reported what she could not conclude. Completing one assessment path would not count the other tasks as performed.

career_archive_assessment_choice.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assessment_choice.text: A stain might invite a dramatic diagnosis. An uncertain attachment might demand a refusal that looked unimpressive. A fitted support might expose every weakness in Yue's measured handwork. All three assignments had valid consent and qualified supervision; none required private text or authority she lacked. She could choose freely, without a stat gate. The independent examiner waited while Yue decided which difficulty she was ready to meet.

choices.text: Record the persistent stain and test the limits of a condition finding.
Assess the uncertain attachment and carry any necessary referral through.
Fit a support for the stable permitted sheet under observation.

career_archive_assess_stain_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_stain_01.text: The stained sheet was a released public reading copy, stable enough for the specified supported observation. The examiner asked whether the brown tide line proved damage during a particular storm. Yue wanted a definite answer because the mark looked so eloquent. She checked the receiving conditions and found no continuous history joining the stain to that storm. Her finding could describe a tide line and present condition. It could not assign an absent date.

career_archive_assess_stain_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_stain_02.text: The authorized record showed the stain already present at this intake, with no approved treatment in Yue's task. She used an ordinary ruler beside the support, avoiding contact with the marked surface, and entered its actual visible extent. Tan supervised the handling. The examiner watched without prompting. Yue felt the old unease of offering something smaller than the question she had been asked, and kept the finding small anyway.

career_archive_assess_stain_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_stain_03.text: A reader at the public desk wanted to know whether the stained copy could still be issued. That decision belonged to Tan's qualified review, not Yue's assessment mark. Tan approved the particular stable copy for the ordinary supported reading arrangement after her examination. The examiner asked Yue to distinguish the permission from her condition description. She did so, then felt oddly disappointed that someone else had supplied the reassuring part.

career_archive_assess_stain_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_stain_04.text: Luo carried the copy to its permitted receiving place after the record was checked. No household claim was rejudged, and the stain was not erased by a good description. The first assessed shift produced one accepted condition record and paid four copper. Yue had earned twenty-four copper across six completed shifts. The examiner's silence made the coin feel suspiciously loud in her pouch.

career_archive_assess_stain_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_stain_05.text: At the second assessed shift, Yue checked the same released copy after its ordinary reading, under renewed handling permission. The tide line had not visibly expanded within the limits of their simple comparison. A new crease appeared at the lower corner. She recorded both facts separately. Stable evidence about one mark did not excuse ignoring another. The reader's identity remained outside the condition entry because the work did not need it.

career_archive_assess_stain_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_stain_06.text: The examiner asked whether Yue would write 'unchanged' across the whole sheet. She pointed to the new crease and declined. After checking the supported placement and the two records, the examiner accepted the completed task. The second assessed shift earned four copper, bringing wages to twenty-eight. Yue had finished seven actual shifts. She knew how much an honest condition report could leave unanswered, and how much effort its modest answer could take.

career_archive_assess_stain_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_stain_07.text: When she finally put down the ruler, her fingers had left a small crescent of sweat on the wooden support, away from the paper. Tan passed her a cloth. The examiner marked the stain-path competence as an accurate bounded comparison with a correctly limited claim. Yue had not cured the stain, dated it or acquired anyone's private history. She had given the next permitted worker a reliable place to begin.

career_archive_assess_referral_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_referral_01.text: The assigned public copy had a loose margin beside an uncertain attachment. Its task permission allowed supported examination but no attempt to dissolve, peel or cut anything. Yue could not identify the material from appearance alone. The examiner asked what she would do before a reader's afternoon booking. The deadline made an answer feel urgent. She marked the limit, stopped that handling operation and requested Tan's qualified examination.

career_archive_assess_referral_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_referral_02.text: Tan confirmed that the attachment should remain undisturbed pending specialist advice. She did not use Yue's referral as a reason to pronounce a convenient cure. The issued copy became unavailable for that afternoon's booking. A sound alternative public text existed, but it was a different text. Luo went to offer that choice to the reader, who had traveled specifically for a passage the alternative did not contain.

career_archive_assess_referral_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_referral_03.text: The reader declined the substitute and asked for another date. Yue heard the conversation from the bench without stepping into the claim that a correct refusal should have satisfied everybody. Luo recorded the actual postponement and made no promise before the specialist's answer. The examiner asked Yue to record what service had been lost. She entered the canceled access to this copy, keeping the person's private reasons outside the condition record.

career_archive_assess_referral_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_referral_04.text: By the first shift's receiving, Yue had completed the observed examination, authorized referral and accurate unavailability notice under supervision. Four copper paid that completed work, bringing her total to twenty-four. The unresolved attachment did not make the work imaginary. Neither did an accepted wage make the attachment resolved. Yue was beginning to understand why a useful trade could contain days that felt like defeats.

career_archive_assess_referral_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_referral_05.text: During the second assessed shift, the specialist sent a written recommendation to the qualified custodian. It authorized a later treatment outside Yue's qualification and outside this trainee task. Yue matched the item identifier to the actual supported copy and prepared an enclosure that left the attachment untouched. Tan checked the fit and stored it under the real collection's custody. No private original had entered the room.

career_archive_assess_referral_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_referral_06.text: The reader received the accurate next available review date, rather than a promised treatment completion. Yue checked that the referral record, temporary enclosure and access notice described the same present situation. The examiner accepted the completed receiving. Another four copper brought her wages to twenty-eight for seven actual shifts. The afternoon she had not saved remained lost. She felt proud of the work and wished pride could make the reader's journey shorter.

career_archive_assess_referral_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_referral_07.text: The examiner recorded the referral-path competence as safe boundary recognition carried through to an honest service consequence. Yue had not earned treatment authority by recognizing a need for treatment. Tan asked what she would improve next time. Yue said she would warn the public desk sooner, before somebody spent a journey on uncertain availability. The examiner wrote that answer down only after Yue explained how it would fit the same permissions.

career_archive_assess_support_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_support_01.text: The assessment sheet was a stable public copy already released for the specified handling. Yue had to fit a support that protected an uneven lower edge during ordinary reading. The examiner supplied the accepted limits and a sound sample board. Tan supervised handling of the copy; the fitting work remained Yue's. Her first measurement looked exact until she remembered the sheet must settle naturally rather than be forced into a handsome rectangle.

career_archive_assess_support_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_support_02.text: She measured the supported profile twice from the same allowed position and noticed that one earlier note used the folder's edge as its reference. Yue corrected her own working sketch before cutting the board. The examiner watched her waste a small offcut already allowed in the materials allocation. Perfect thrift could have produced a tight fit. A real offcut was cheaper than a corner strained to justify it.

career_archive_assess_support_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_support_03.text: When the fitted support arrived under the copy, the irregular edge remained free of pressure. Yue checked its stops without moving the paper beyond permission. Tan examined the arrangement and approved the particular reading use. Yue recorded the shape and its limits so another permitted worker could replace the support correctly. The support did not repair the edge; it changed how this sound-enough copy could be used.

career_archive_assess_support_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_support_04.text: The first assessed shift ended after the fit, condition entry and authorized receiving were checked. Four copper brought Yue's wages to twenty-four. At the public desk, the first reader preferred to prop the copy against a bag. Luo explained the support and offered the accepted reading position. The reader agreed reluctantly. Yue discovered that making useful things included leaving people room to dislike their inconvenience.

career_archive_assess_support_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_support_05.text: The second assessed shift checked the support after ordinary use. One outer stop had shifted slightly without touching the sheet. Yue removed the copy only under Tan's immediate handling supervision and corrected the stop at the empty bench. She then repeated the approved placement. The examiner asked why she had not tightened the fitting while the sheet stayed in place. The answer involved an avoidable risk, not the appearance of confidence.

career_archive_assess_support_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_support_06.text: Yue completed the corrected fit, second condition check and receiving record. The examiner accepted the work, and the wage clerk paid four copper. Twenty-eight copper now covered seven completed shifts. Yue had not gained custody of the sheet or permission to read beyond public access. She had earned the satisfaction of an ugly little support that did exactly what the uneven edge required.

career_archive_assess_support_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assess_support_07.text: The examiner entered the support-path competence as a fitted, checked arrangement with a properly controlled correction after use. Tan returned the released copy to its appointed custody. Yue kept only her permitted blank measurements and her own working drawing. It looked less elegant than the model she had imagined before the assessment. She liked it better now that she knew which awkward angle had kept a real corner free.

career_archive_assessment_history.speaker: narrator
career_archive_assessment_history.text: The independent examiner next reviewed the teaching record, including the actual trial result and any later remediation. A qualification could not depend on concealing how Yue had learned. The examiner asked her to describe a moment when her wish to appear ready had differed from what she could safely demonstrate. Yue looked at her own notebook, which remained hers, and chose an answer grounded in the practice path she had actually taken.

career_archive_history_failure.speaker: narrator
career_archive_history_failure.text: Yue described the unsupported practice lift, the tear and the extra supervised interval her remediation had used. She showed how the later exercise had changed her actual sequence of checks. The examiner retained the first failure beside the later demonstrated pass. It neither barred her forever nor disappeared to make the certificate look cleaner. Tan had spent real cover time teaching that correction; Yue named it without apologizing for having needed teaching.

career_archive_history_stop.speaker: narrator
career_archive_history_stop.text: Yue described stopping before the doubtful edge, leaving the lift requirement incomplete and later testing a stable practice blank within a verifiable limit. The examiner retained both results. Caution had protected the first sheet, while a different completed exercise had supplied the missing demonstration. She had not required an extra remediation interval. Yue could now explain that distinction without pretending she had never been tempted to wait forever.

career_archive_history_support.speaker: narrator
career_archive_history_support.text: Yue described Tan holding the first support, her correctly bounded supported attempt and the later independent practice fitting. The examiner named Tan's contribution in the reviewed result. The supported success did not become solo experience just because Yue now worked more confidently. Her qualification would rest on what the later assessment itself demonstrated. She was grateful to the teacher and unexpectedly grateful for a record that prevented gratitude from becoming vague.

career_archive_qualification_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_qualification_01.text: The examiner asked about the conditions that would invalidate Yue's demonstrated method: uncertain stability, missing permission, unexpected resistance or work beyond the assistant scope. Yue gave examples from completed tasks without claiming she had performed the alternative assessment paths. Tan stayed out of the marking discussion. For once Yue wished the teacher would interrupt. Waiting for a judgment she could not influence was harder than waiting for rain to stop.

career_archive_qualification_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_qualification_02.text: After reviewing the actual work and the correction or referral record, the independent examiner passed Yue for the condition-record assistant qualification. The board issued its bounded certificate under the existing examiner allocation. Tan shook her hand instead of touching the paper first. Yue felt a sudden ridiculous urge to run outside and show the plum tree. She settled for reading her own name three times.

career_archive_qualification_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_qualification_03.text: The certificate authorized listed assistant duties within valid item permissions and required qualified referral for unstable paper or treatment. It did not make Yue a licensed conservation-treatment practitioner. It conferred no private access, family custody or cultivation rank. Her fifth stage remained earned exactly as before. She could now apply for those assistant duties with evidence other than wanting them. That small legal difference made a large difference to her future.

career_archive_qualification_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_qualification_04.text: Luo asked whether she wanted the public desk to announce the pass. Yue agreed to her name and qualification title being posted, without any private letters or assessment items displayed. Sun read the notice and said its lettering looked anxious. Yue admitted she had written it herself. Sun congratulated her, then asked whether the newly qualified person could help shorten a kite tail. Yue had to ask whose permission she needed.

career_archive_qualification_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_qualification_05.text: The child agreed to lend the spare blank kite paper for a demonstration at last, then watched every fold critically. Yue used ordinary craft work outside collection handling and returned the unused sheet. The kite rose, lurched and found an uneven sort of balance. Nobody entered it as conservation evidence. Tan leaned against the courtyard wall and laughed when its owner declared the tail only 'provisionally adequate.'

career_archive_qualification_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_qualification_06.text: At final assessment receiving, the independent examiner's twelve copper paid the completed evaluation. Twenty-eight copper had paid Yue's seven finished shifts; the last twelve wage copper remained for three real specialty shifts. The twelve-copper materials line and twenty-four-copper qualified-cover allocation retained their actual purpose. The twelve reserve copper stayed unspent. Earlier trial choices had affected teaching time and recorded learning, without creating wages for exercises.

career_archive_qualification_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_qualification_07.text: Yue completed the accepted qualification receiving by matching the certificate's scope to the actual task records and making sure the delayed, stained or supported item retained its real present condition. This last check formed part of the already paid assessed work. The demonstrated persistence was recorded as growth only now, after the work had been completed. A passed certificate did not turn an unfinished service into a finished one.

career_archive_qualification_08.speaker: narrator
career_archive_qualification_08.text: The three remaining shifts could deepen one practical specialty: routine moisture watch, fitted enclosures or supported reader access. The board funded one supervised placement, not all three. Each used the same remaining trainee wages and existing cover allocation, with different work for the people waiting. Yue could choose any specialty within her new scope. Becoming qualified had opened a door; it had not multiplied the hours on the other side.

career_archive_specialty_choice.speaker: narrator
career_archive_specialty_choice.text: The moisture-watch placement would catch changing conditions but leave fewer new enclosures. The enclosure bench would reduce handling strain but leave the extended watch unfilled. Supported access would help readers use permitted copies while deferring both projects. Existing minimum checks and urgent qualified referrals continued regardless. The three-shift placement could improve one service. Yue had to choose which everyday loss she would be willing to see afterward.

choices.text: Develop the moisture-watch specialty and keep its recurring rounds.
Develop fitted enclosures for the waiting stable public copies.
Develop supported reader access in the accepted public hours.

career_archive_watch_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_watch_01.text: Yue chose the recurring moisture-watch rounds. The first specialty shift began at the public-copy cabinet, whose ordinary minimum checks already continued. Her added work paired the accepted room readings with visible condition observations on specifically permitted stable copies. It could reveal change sooner; it could not diagnose unseen damage or authorize opening private packets. Tan showed her the dull corner where useful instruments waited. Yue found its lack of grandeur oddly inviting.

career_archive_watch_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_watch_02.text: A window seal had lifted above the cabinet. Yue saw a small change in the simple room reading before any visible paper swelling. She reported the actual values and the loose seal to Tan, without claiming a future disaster. The qualified custodian moved the released public stock under its existing permission, while the ordinary maintenance worker repaired the seal under the archive's routine arrangements. Yue did not repair a roof by writing a number.

career_archive_watch_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_watch_03.text: After checking the record and receiving the moved public stock, Tan accepted the first shift's completed rounds. Four copper brought Yue's wages to thirty-two. The condition remained under qualified review rather than declared cured. At lunch Luo asked how she liked the specialty. She said it involved watching a room breathe. He said she must avoid putting that sentence on the public instrument log. She agreed, keeping it for the letter she would write home.

career_archive_watch_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_watch_04.text: The second shift's rounds occupied the early interval when the enclosure bench normally had its quietest light. The waiting folders would not all be made during this placement. A reader complained that her public copy still traveled in its old, serviceable wrapper. Yue could explain the chosen work without making the reader grateful for its priority. Tan kept unsafe items from issue under ordinary rules; inconvenience alone did not make every old wrapper unsafe.

career_archive_watch_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_watch_05.text: Yue completed the second rounds, noticed no further change at the repaired window and recorded that limited result. Tan accepted the checked observations, and another four copper brought wages to thirty-six. In the courtyard Sun asked whether Yue now trusted windows less. Yue said she trusted them in more specific ways. Sun looked at the plum tree and said that sounded useful for people too, provided nobody mistook a habit of checking for affection.

career_archive_watch_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_watch_06.text: The third shift included the inconvenient evening round. Yue had wanted to share supper with Luo and the child who owned the kite. The contract's actual hours placed her at the cabinet then, with qualified cover still present. She ate earlier and heard the supper laughter through the door. Stable paid work could cost moments she had wanted, even when nothing went wrong. The thought of a permanent rota became both comforting and heavy.

career_archive_watch_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_watch_07.text: Before the round ended, Yue identified a small fresh curl on one permitted public copy and stopped its issue for Tan's examination. The qualified custodian isolated that copy and retained the judgment about its use. Yue finished the accepted record and handover. Four copper paid the third specialty shift, bringing her ten-shift wages to forty. The curl remained real. Her careful watch had made an earlier referral possible, not reversed the paper's change.

career_archive_watch_08.speaker: narrator
career_archive_watch_08.text: Tan signed the completed moisture-watch placement with the actual early referral and evening round named. Yue's checked observations had improved her insight through performed work. The assistant qualification retained its existing limits. The waiting enclosure batch remained deferred, and the ordinary supported reading desk had gained no extra trainee hours. Yue was beginning to see a career as a repeated choice about whose inconvenient tomorrow would become her own morning.

career_archive_enclosures_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_enclosures_01.text: Yue chose fitted enclosures for stable public copies waiting in their serviceable older wrappers. The first specialty shift began with an authorized batch and Tan's stability review. Damaged or uncertain items stayed outside Yue's handling scope. The added batch could reduce everyday strain for these copies; it could not restore lost annotations or create private access. Yue liked the visible work and distrusted herself a little for liking a result people could hold.

career_archive_enclosures_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_enclosures_02.text: The first folder needed an awkward allowance around a thickened binding. Yue cut the allocated stock from a blank template rather than press the copy flat. Tan checked the fit after supervised placement. A public reader called the folder lopsided. Yue explained the uneven binding and stopped short of arguing that good work must be beautiful. She had once fired a cup with a crooked lip that her family used for years.

career_archive_enclosures_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_enclosures_03.text: At receiving, the accepted first batch and its condition entries earned four copper. Yue's total reached thirty-two. She rubbed an imaginary straight line from her template and realized she was trying to correct the drawing rather than the folder. Tan asked if the copy had acquired a straighter binding while she looked away. Yue laughed and left the template honest. Its ugly corner would help the next worker fit another one correctly.

career_archive_enclosures_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_enclosures_04.text: The second shift used a quiet bench interval instead of the added moisture rounds. Ordinary minimum cabinet checks continued, and no unsafe issue was permitted; the extra comparison visit would remain unfilled during this placement. Luo could not promise readers that every environmental change would now be noticed sooner. Yue had chosen one improvement with bounded resources. She felt that tradeoff most sharply when the work itself went well.

career_archive_enclosures_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_enclosures_05.text: A pair of stable reading copies received fitted folders and clear replacement guides under their existing permissions. Tan checked the supports and accepted the second batch. Four copper brought wages to thirty-six. The child with the kite asked for a folder shaped like a fish. Yue drew a fish on her own scrap and kept the public folders plain. The child accused the archive of wasting excellent fish potential, which was hard to deny.

career_archive_enclosures_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_enclosures_06.text: The third shift's final folder used the last measured stock assigned to this batch. A different reader requested a decorative tab that would need more material and another accepted scope. Yue explained the limit and offered the existing plain label arrangement. The reader withdrew the request without becoming friendly. Yue finished the fit and wondered how often earning a dependable livelihood would mean refusing a small pleasure she could almost provide.

career_archive_enclosures_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_enclosures_07.text: Tan accepted the final enclosures, placement checks and replacement guides. Four copper paid the third specialty shift, bringing Yue's ten-shift wages to forty. The copies remained public copies under their actual custody; the folders did not change access terms. Yue held the emptied stock roll and felt a clean satisfaction. She had made a finite set of things, every one connected to a particular edge and a particular permission.

career_archive_enclosures_08.speaker: narrator
career_archive_enclosures_08.text: The completed enclosure placement demonstrated steadier measured work and controlled corrections, earning resolve through those actual tasks. The assistant certificate retained its bounded scope. The extra moisture rounds and added reader-support hours had not been performed. Tan signed the specialty record while Yue watched the lopsided folder settle comfortably around its lopsided copy. She wanted more of this trade, and knew wanting it would mean choosing its neglected neighboring work again.

career_archive_access_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_access_01.text: Yue chose supported reader access during the accepted public hours. The first specialty shift used stable public copies that Tan had already approved for specified supports. Confidential papers and private family notebooks remained outside the desk. Yue's job was to set up and hand over permitted material safely, explain the support and record present condition. Reader questions about claims or restricted text still belonged with the proper public-reference or private-review staff.

career_archive_access_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_access_02.text: An elderly reader disliked the low support because it changed the position she used at home. Yue asked Tan to check an ordinary adjustable stand against the permitted arrangement, rather than improvise pressure against the copy. The qualified custodian approved a suitable position for this stable item. The reader could finally see comfortably. Yue did not learn the woman's family history in exchange for helping her look at a public page.

career_archive_access_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_access_03.text: The first shift ended after accepted placements, reader handovers and receiving checks. Four copper brought Yue's wages to thirty-two. She found the work louder than the bench, full of chair legs and interruptions. Luo asked if that made her regret the choice. She admitted she had enjoyed being thanked where she could hear it. He said liking thanks was ordinary; arranging work only to obtain it would be harder on the readers.

career_archive_access_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_access_04.text: The second shift's added public hours replaced the funded specialty time that could have gone to new folders or extra moisture rounds. Existing minimum condition checks and qualified referrals continued. The old serviceable wrappers stayed in use where Tan allowed them. A young reader arrived early to secure a supported seat, and Yue understood why this specialty mattered. The people waiting at the other benches still had reasons just as good.

career_archive_access_05.speaker: narrator
career_archive_access_05.text: Yue completed a difficult handover when a reader wanted to leave a supported copy open during the lunch closure. She explained the actual desk hours, received the copy safely and offered the next accepted session. The reader objected, then returned later. Tan checked the completed condition entries, and four copper brought wages to thirty-six. Yue had maintained a boundary without making compliance proof that the person trusted her.

career_archive_access_06.speaker: narrator
career_archive_access_06.text: On the third shift, Sun used a permitted public text and asked Yue to help place the support, under its accepted access. Her private notebook stayed home. Sun chose to stop after a short sitting and took her own personal notes away. Yue did not convert the visit into an oral-history session. Familiarity with Sun had once made everything feel easier. Here it made an ordinary stopping request feel especially important to honor.

career_archive_access_07.speaker: narrator
career_archive_access_07.text: At final receiving, every accepted public copy was back under its proper custody, with the actual condition checks complete. Four copper paid the third specialty shift and brought ten-shift wages to forty. The extra seats had served their real readers during these hours only. No further public timetable had been promised. Yue felt tired in a sociable way, full of other people's ordinary impatience and the pleasure of helping them get on with their day.

career_archive_access_08.speaker: narrator
career_archive_access_08.text: The completed supported-access placement demonstrated reliable permissions, clear boundaries and actual safe handovers, earning trust through performed work. Her assistant qualification did not acquire privacy authority. New enclosure production and the added watch remained deferred during this placement. Luo signed the desk's actual receiving alongside Tan's handling review. Yue wanted a career with people in it, and had discovered that people sometimes thanked her most after she had told them a patient, useful no.

career_archive_future_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_future_01.text: The trainee term's final account paid forty copper for Yue's ten completed shifts, twelve for the completed independent examination, twelve for the purchased board stock, folder paper and teaching cloth, and twenty-four for the delivered qualified cover. Eighty-eight copper had been spent from the one-hundred-copper appropriation. The unused twelve-copper reserve returned to its board account. No old winter purse, household compensation or reading-service grant had supported this appointment.

career_archive_future_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_future_02.text: Tan filed the assistant qualification and the actual selected placement under their agreed access. Yue retained her own wage receipts, certificate copy and private notebook. The record named any failed trial, supported contribution or incomplete first exercise accurately. Family originals and Sun's notebook stayed with their custodians. Becoming useful in the archive had not made the collection hers. She was relieved by that limit and still occasionally tempted to forget it.

career_archive_future_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_future_03.text: At the next ordinary receiving, the board considered new specialty contracts with separate appropriations and named future scopes. Yue's completed placement would determine which supervised assistant rota she could join first without another specialty induction. The other services still needed their own people or future training. This was no automatic permanent appointment or payment. It was the practical consequence of where she had spent her three deepening shifts.

career_archive_future_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_future_04.text: Luo brought the actual roster to the courtyard after receiving. Tan had marked which selected specialty the completed work supported, and which neighboring projects remained unfilled. Yue did not get three futures simply because she could imagine all of them. A kite flickered over the wall and fell out of sight with an indignant shout. She looked at the roster again, ready to find out what her chosen work had left behind.

career_archive_outcome_watch_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_watch_01.text: The moisture-watch roster offered Yue the first separately funded assistant rounds, under continuing qualified cover, because she had completed that specialty. The next term would require its own accepted contract before any wages were due. The earlier fresh curl had remained referred; Tan's later decision kept that copy out of issue pending qualified work. Yue's watch had changed when the problem was known, not guaranteed that the paper could return.

career_archive_outcome_watch_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_watch_02.text: The deferred enclosure batch still used its older approved wrappers. One reader had to wait while an attendant arranged a suitable existing support. The extra public-support hours had also remained absent. Yue saw the inconvenience instead of describing every unused hour as disaster prevented. The chosen specialty had produced earlier information and a steadier watch. It had not secretly performed the competing improvements while she was busy.

career_archive_outcome_watch_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_watch_03.text: Luo asked whether the recurring evening round would fit the life she wanted. Yue thought of the missed supper and the satisfying little record at the loose window. She asked for the proposed hours in writing before considering the new appointment. Her newly demonstrated insight made her a credible candidate for this rota; it did not make every offered schedule bearable. She would still have to choose how much ordinary life the trade could take.

career_archive_outcome_watch_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_watch_04.text: Sun stopped at the courtyard to hear the unseen bird again. Yue stood with her before returning to the roster. The archive's windows would need watching whether she took the next contract or not, and the folder queue would still need somebody else. She had developed a real specialty whose future work and omissions remained visible. The certificate in her pouch felt less like an ending now, and more like a weight she had chosen carefully.

career_archive_outcome_enclosures_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_enclosures_01.text: The enclosure roster offered Yue the first separately funded assistant fitting batch because she had completed that specialty under qualification. A new contract would still need agreed scope and hours before wages became due. The fitted public copies from her placement remained usable under their actual access arrangements. Their enclosures reduced ordinary handling strain; they did not repair the damaged items Tan had kept outside Yue's scope.

career_archive_outcome_enclosures_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_enclosures_02.text: The added moisture-watch slot remained unfilled, with ordinary minimum checks continuing. At a later routine check, Tan found a small curl on one copy and referred it for qualified review. Yue could not claim her enclosure placement had supplied an earlier warning. The extra reader-support hours were also absent, so one reader waited for the ordinary desk session. The folders had helped particular copies while those neighboring improvements remained undone.

career_archive_outcome_enclosures_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_enclosures_03.text: The new fitting batch included the uneven sort of binding Yue had learned to accommodate. Luo asked whether she wanted the work. She asked for the actual stock allowance and receiving deadline first, remembering the nearly possible decorative tab. Resolve had made her a credible candidate for this bench, not a person without limits. She wanted to build things that served their owners rather than spend every evening repairing promises she had made too quickly.

career_archive_outcome_enclosures_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_enclosures_04.text: Sun admired the ugly folder without asking to own it. Yue told her why its corner looked that way, using only the public item's permitted condition. A gust tugged the kite above the wall, and somebody cheered at the improbable angle of its flight. Yue watched the folder sit quietly on the roster table. She had learned a specialty that made small objects dependable, while its unchosen hours kept asking for other hands.

career_archive_outcome_access_01.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_access_01.text: The supported-access roster offered Yue the first separately funded assistant desk sessions because she had completed that specialty. Any future wage required a new agreed contract and actual service. The earlier readers had received their permitted copies in safe arrangements, including Sun's short sitting and the elder reader's adjusted stand. Yue's work had changed those visits without opening confidential shelves or making personal stories a fee for assistance.

career_archive_outcome_access_02.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_access_02.text: The enclosure queue remained in its older approved wrappers, and the added moisture-watch slot remained unfilled. A later ordinary condition check found a small curl on one copy; Tan referred it and retained the use decision. Yue could not claim the public desk hours had found it earlier. A reader still waited while an attendant located a suitable existing support. Real access had improved for one group without dissolving the neighboring work.

career_archive_outcome_access_03.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_access_03.text: The proposed desk rota included an afternoon when Yue had hoped to travel home. Luo asked whether she could cover it. She asked him to keep the offered date explicit while she checked her plans, rather than volunteer from gratitude and regret it later. Earned trust had made her a credible candidate for this service. It did not entitle the archive to her private hours or oblige readers to prefer her over another trained attendant.

career_archive_outcome_access_04.speaker: narrator
career_archive_outcome_access_04.text: Sun paused beside the plum tree and asked what Yue liked best about the work. Yue said helping someone get far enough into a permitted page to forget the support beneath it. Sun nodded, then said she still preferred a well-positioned chair. Yue laughed. Her specialty would keep bringing her people with priorities of their own. The future felt less flattering than a heroic title and more inviting than she had expected.

career_archive_finish.speaker: narrator
career_archive_finish.text: Yue left the roster with its actual offers, deferred projects and unpaid future scopes intact. Her forty copper belonged to ten completed work shifts; her assistant qualification belonged to independently assessed tasks. The chosen specialty had supplied a credible next career step, with its lasting costs still visible. Her earned fifth stage had not changed. She tucked the certificate beside her private letters and went to meet the others, carrying a future she could develop rather than a promise already fulfilled.
